root_cause.text: `sch_teql` allowed TEQL to be instantiated as a non-root/classful qdisc, even though it only maintains correct queue length state when used as the root qdisc, which let its `peek()`/`dequeue()` behavior break parent qdisc accounting and lead to a use-after-free in `qfq` during class reconfiguration.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (sch->parent != TC_H_ROOT) { ... return -EOPNOTSUPP; }` in `teql_qdisc_init()`, and the CVE description explains that TEQL under a `QFQ` class kept `sch->q.qlen` at 0 because its qlen is only updated at dequeue while `peek()` always returns NULL, causing `qfq_change_class()`/`qfq_deact_rm_from_agg()` to free aggregate pointers and later dereference a dangling pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject non-root TEQL qdisc setup by adding an explicit parent-hierarchy check with an extack error.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added in `teql_qdisc_init()` after the existing loopback-device check. The code now tests whether `sch->parent != TC_H_ROOT`, and if so it sets an extack error message (`"teql can only be used as root"`) and returns `-EOPNOTSUPP` before continuing with initialization.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents TEQL qdiscs from being created anywhere except at the root of the traffic control hierarchy. If a caller tries to attach TEQL as a child qdisc, initialization now fails early with a clear error message instead of proceeding.

grouping_result.intent: Reject non-root TEQL qdisc setup by adding an explicit parent-hierarchy check with an extack error.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by preventing TEQL from being instantiated as a non-root/classful qdisc, which is exactly the unsafe configuration that led to incorrect queue accounting and the downstream use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This assignment completes TEQL qdisc setup without any check that it is being attached as the root qdisc. Because TEQL only maintains correct queue length state in root position, allowing setup to proceed here enables the invalid non-root/classful instantiation that later breaks accounting and can contribute to the qfq use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line completes TEQL qdisc setup without enforcing that TEQL is only used as the root qdisc. The root cause is that TEQL must not be instantiated as a non-root/classful qdisc because its queue-length accounting is only correct in root position; allowing setup to proceed here enables the invalid configuration that later breaks parent qdisc accounting and can lead to the qfq use-after-free.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the qdisc implementation and initialization path for TEQL. The vulnerable construct is present: `teql_qdisc_init()` accepts any device and attaches the qdisc without enforcing root-only/classless use. In particular, it simply does `q->m = m; skb_queue_head_init(&q->q);` and then links the instance into `m->slaves` / `NEXT_SLAVE(m->slaves) = sch;` with no check that the qdisc is being installed only as the root qdisc. The dequeue logic also depends on root-style accounting: `teql_dequeue()` updates `sch->q.qlen = dat->q.qlen + dat->m->dev->qdisc->q.qlen;`, which assumes the device's qdisc/accounting model of the master/root setup. There is no fix here preventing non-root/classful instantiation, so the vulnerable condition exists and the corrective restriction is absent.
